paras: The Warren settlement-dispute killings were the reported killing of one Black man and the mortal wounding of another in Arkansas shortly before mid-January 1888, after a "squad" went to a Black man's house following a debt dispute with a white man named Gorman. The only account, a short item in an Arkansas news column, rested on rumor and named none of the dead, the wounded or the attackers.

According to the item, the trouble "grew out of a settlement" between a Black man and Gorman, at which the Black man was found to be indebted to Gorman and "there were some hard words." The Black man, with several others, then visited Gorman's house twice.

Word of the killing reached Warren on a Friday morning, with the killing placed on the night before; the item does not give a calendar date, but its first printing on 14 January places it earlier in the month. "Rumor says," the item continued, that a squad went to the Black man's house and that in "the difficulty that followed" one Black man was killed and another mortally wounded. One report added that a white man had been "dangerously cut with a knife."
The item's count of the dead is inconsistent: its opening sentence speaks of "the killing of two negroes," while its body describes one man killed and a second mortally wounded.
No report of an inquest, arrest or later death of the wounded man appears in the coverage.

The Forrest City Times printed the story as one paragraph in its "About Arkansas" column on 14 January 1888 and reran the same text, word for word, in the column on 21 January. The paragraph sat among items on crop prices, railway contracts and other shootings, and it hedged each step with "it seems," "rumor says" and "one report says," without comment on the killing. It identified the dead only as "negroes" and gave no race for the squad.

accounts.label: Arkansas state-news column (rumor)
accounts.gist: After a debt settlement and hard words, a Black man and several others visited Gorman's house twice; rumor said a squad then went to the Black man's house, where one Black man was killed, another mortally wounded, and, by one report, a white man badly cut.

framing.detail: A one-paragraph item in the Forrest City Times 'About Arkansas' column, hedged with 'it seems', 'rumor says' and 'one report says', run on 14 January and again on 21 January.

versions.value: One negro killed and another mortally wounded

conflicts.note: Both versions are in the same item: the opening sentence counts two killed, the body one dead and one mortally wounded.

record_check.dossier: Before 14 January 1888: the item first ran on 14 January and dates the killing only to the Thursday night before a Friday report at Warren.
No county is stated; the item names only Warren, in an Arkansas column.
One report says a white man was dangerously cut with a knife (one unconfirmed report).
One killed and one mortally wounded in the body; the opening sentence says two killed.
Two printings in the same paper, first on 1888-01-14.
'A squad', per rumor; members, number and race not stated.

info: On a Thursday night before 14 January 1888 (the night before a Friday on which the report reached Warren); the exact date is not given
